working: Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate (1 + 2i sin t): the quotient becomes ((3 - 4 sin^2 t) + 8i sin t)/(1 + 4 sin^2 t). It is real exactly when 8 sin t = 0, i.e. sin t = 0. On 0 < t < 2pi the only such value is t = pi. Checked all four options numerically: pi gives 3 (real); pi/6 gives 1 + 2i; pi/3 gives 1.732i; pi/2 gives -0.2 + 1.6i.
notes: rationalising gives numerator 3 - 4sin^2(theta) + 8i*sin(theta), so the imaginary part vanishes only when sin(theta) = 0. The single value in 0 < theta < 2pi is pi

working: Write a = e^(i alpha), b = e^(i beta), c = e^(i gamma), each of unit modulus. Then b/c + c/a + a/b = e^(i(beta-gamma)) + e^(i(gamma-alpha)) + e^(i(alpha-beta)), whose imaginary part is exactly sin(beta-gamma) + sin(gamma-alpha) + sin(alpha-beta) — the same sum the question asks for, just reordered. The given value 1 is real, so that imaginary part must be 0.

(1+i)^n/(1-i)^(n-2) = [(1+i)/(1-i)]^n * (1-i)^2. Since (1+i)/(1-i) = i and (1-i)^2 = -2i, the expression equals i^n * (-2i) = -2 i^(n+1). Evaluated both sides for n = 1,2,3,4,5,7,10,-3: option C matched at every value while A, B and D failed (e.g. n=1 gives 2, and -2 i^2 = 2, whereas -i^0 = -1).

Modulus of 3/2 + i sqrt(3)/2 is sqrt(9/4 + 3/4) = sqrt(3); argument is arctan((sqrt3/2)/(3/2)) = pi/6. So the 50th power is (sqrt3)^50 * e^(i*50pi/6) = 3^25 * e^(i*25pi/3), and 25pi/3 - 8pi = pi/3. Hence x + iy = e^(i pi/3) = 1/2 + i sqrt(3)/2. Verified numerically: (1.5 + 0.8660i)^50 / 3^25 = 0.5 + 0.86603i.

working: The line x = 4y - 2 is y = (x+2)/4 and the parabola is y = x^2/4. Setting them equal gives x^2 = x + 2, so x = -1 and x = 2. Area = (1/4) * integral from -1 to 2 of (x + 2 - x^2) dx = (1/4)(9/2) = 9/8. Confirmed by numeric integration over 2,000,000 strips: 1.1250000.

working: From the shared context alpha + beta = -b/a and alpha*beta = c/a. For a^3 x^2 + abc x + c^3 = 0 the root sum is -bc/a^2 and the product is c^3/a^3. Option A gives sum alpha*beta(alpha+beta) = (c/a)(-b/a) = -bc/a^2 and product (alpha*beta)^3 = c^3/a^3 — both match. alpha + beta = -b/a = sin t + cos t and alpha*beta = c/a = sin t cos t. Squaring the first, b^2/a^2 = 1 + 2c/a, so b^2 = a^2 + 2ac. Then b^2 + c^2 = a^2 + 2ac + c^2 = (a+c)^2, which is option D. Tested numerically at three awkward angles (t = 0.37, 1.13, 2.90 rad) and with a = 2.7 as well as a = 1: D held to machine precision every time, while A, B and C each failed.
notes: with sin(theta) and cos(theta) as the roots of ax^2+bx+c, the sum is -b/a and the product c/a. Squaring the sum: b^2/a^2 = 1 + 2c/a, so b^2 = a^2 + 2ac. Then (a+c)^2 = a^2 + 2ac + c^2 = b^2 + c^2, which is option D. Option A fails unless c = 2a, so it is not an identity

working: Since a*alpha^2 + b*alpha + c = 0, alpha(a*alpha + b) = -c, so 1/(a*alpha + b) = -alpha/c, and likewise for beta. Sum of the new roots = -(alpha+beta)/c = b/(ac); product = alpha*beta/c^2 = 1/(ac). The monic equation x^2 - (b/ac)x + 1/(ac) = 0 clears to ac*x^2 - bx + 1 = 0, which is option A. Verified by computing 1/(a*alpha+b), 1/(a*beta+b) directly for (a,b,c) = (2,-5,3), (1,7,5), (3,2,-4) and matching them against the roots of each option — A matched all three, B gave the negatives, C gave unrelated values.

From x^2 - px - q = 0: u + v = p and uv = -q. I is correct — reversing the coefficients gives -q x^2 - p x + 1 = 0, i.e. q x^2 + p x - 1 = 0, whose root sum -p/q equals (u+v)/(uv) and whose root product -1/q equals 1/(uv). II is correct — (x-p)(x+q) = 0 has roots p and -q, which are precisely u+v and uv. III is FALSE — the equation with roots u^2, v^2 is x^2 - (p^2+2q)x + q^2 = 0, not x^2 + p^2 x + q^2 = 0, since u^2 + v^2 = p^2 + 2q, not -p^2. Checked with (p,q) = (1,1), (3,-2), (-4,5): I and II matched every time, III never did (e.g. p=3,q=-2 gives u^2,v^2 = 1,4 while the stated equation has roots -8.53 and -0.47).

Then y=x^2 f(x)=(4x^3+5x^2-3x)/14 and dy/dx=(12x^2+10x-3)/14, which at x=-1 is (12-10-3)/14 = -1/14. Verified in sympy: the solved f satisfies the original equation identically (residual 0).

The 8 consonants (with R twice) plus the block give 9!/2! = 181440 arrangements, and the block's internal order gives 4!/3! = 4. Total 181440 x 4 = 725760.

Leading digit must be 3,4,5 or 6 (4 ways) and each of the other three places is free among the six digits: 4 x 6^3 = 864. Confirmed by exhaustively enumerating all 6^4 strings and counting those > 3000 (864). Option D, 1296 = 6^4, is the count with no lower bound at all.

working: Put t = log10 x and take log10 of both sides (valid and order-preserving for x > 0): t(t^2 - 3t + 1) > 3, i.e. t^3 - 3t^2 + t - 3 > 0, which factors as (t-3)(t^2+1) > 0.
